Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.BlockTh.title: Where the congruence bound comes from
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.BlockTh.text: Read IsRankRPart over the fraction field as the decomposition of the lift into a rank-$r$ summand $\rho$ and the prescribed characters. The Selmer term sPi uses $\rho$ twisted by the inverse of the first character, with coefficients in the quotient of the fraction-field space by its lattice.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.title: Where the proof spends the cohomological bound
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.text: The tuple from vvRecord has three components. The proof uses finiteness to apply the link estimate, passes summability to divinN_at, and passes the numerical bound to that lemma after enlarging it to $b$.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.title: What the cohomological length measures
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.text: For each prime $\ell$ and twist $1\le e<t$, the first clause requires finite $\mathbb Z_\ell$-length for the classes that restrict to zero at every place above $\ell$. In the second clause, toNat reads those finite lengths as integers before the sum over an arbitrary finite set of primes.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.title: The two prime choices
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.text: Fix the modulus, $\varepsilon$ and the window exponent before reading the large-$Y$ quantifier. Each $Y$ gets one pair that works throughout its window. The existence proof picks $q$ from a nonempty set of first primes, then $d$ from a nonempty set that depends on that $q$.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.title: The construction behind supplyChi
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Charac.text: The goal left by the call to supplyOfAdm is to supply admissible ranks. The proof substitutes the scale's value of $\varepsilon$, then uses admissibleClassesTwistedChar to obtain ranks with the required sizes and admissibility for the input field.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Dedeki.title: The positive weights in the family
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Dedeki.text: The positivity in `CharFamily` applies to the weights on the characters. The real summands that `Gm` adds, and its prime-power coefficients, may have either sign. The last line calls `windowHyp_of_rpow` to turn the one-sided bound into the integral hypothesis needed by `lemmaL`.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Dedeki.title: The two cases of the pole argument
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Dedeki.text: Read the two patterns after `rcases` as geometric conditions on the poles. The first gives a pole-free disk at the real center $\sigma$ and a pole whose horizontal distance from $\sigma$ is smaller than the disk’s radius. The second gives a disk at $\sigma$ containing just one pole, on the real axis.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Dedeki.title: Why the argument is windowed
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Dedeki.text: Line 88 gets the estimate that will serve both branches. For each requested lower cutoff it gives a later log-window start $U$ and one differentiation order $k\ge U$. The same $k$ works for every vertical shift, which lets the next lines choose the shift after inspecting the poles.

Formalism.HarderNarasimhan.HarderNarasim.title: How the cut rank is bounded
Formalism.HarderNarasimhan.HarderNarasim.text: Count each entry below $s-\tau$ as a deficit of at least $u+\tau$ from the common upper bound $s+u$. The mean bound allows a total deficit of at most $u$ times the number of entries. In the next lemma, counting slopes below the cut gives the rank lost at the filtration step.

Formalism.HarderNarasimhan.StatementFram.title: Theorem F and its sharper form
Formalism.HarderNarasimhan.StatementFram.text: In lines 61–62, `muDef` is the target lattice’s mean slope. Compare the conclusion with `TheoremFSharp` in the same file. The proof of `theoremF_of_sharp` obtains the displayed version by subtracting $\log |I|$ from the sharp lower bound, since the nonempty index set has $|I|\ge 1$.

Formalism.SharpRestriction.Divisibility..title: The exact integrality statement
Formalism.SharpRestriction.Divisibility..text: For each allowed pair of inputs $\phi,F$, the equality supplies a coefficient-field value for the column period. If this value is nonzero, its valuation is at least the rounded exponent used to divide the lattice at $w$.

Formalism.SizeWindowBrackets.ChainSlopeW.title: Where the two main terms agree
Formalism.SizeWindowBrackets.ChainSlopeW.text: `Lam5` is the lower bound for the logarithm of the level in `Count5`. It includes the counting error with a minus sign, so subtracting `sumA` times `Lam5` gives the added error on the right. The proof unfolds `Lam5` and obtains the equality by a linear combination of the earlier `key_identity`.

Formalism.SizeWindowBrackets.SChain.title: Where ChainTied gets the eleven clauses
Formalism.SizeWindowBrackets.SChain.text: Unfold this proposition to see the eleven clauses imposed on one chain datum at the chosen scale. ChainTied supplies them together, and each_unit_bound_statement uses them to bound ASK by the sum of a main term and an error for each outer index.
